finding: The review arm reads role attribution "from the `role` field the output contract stamps on each recorded row", but a recorded review round is the merged file copied verbatim by `--record`, and `tp review --merge` emits one cluster **representative** per (location, class): the losing rows are discarded and their roles survive only in the `found_by_roles` array the merge adds. A role that co-reported a blocking finding therefore carries no `role` stamp on the surviving row and is not blocked — which is exactly the loophole §2.6 exists to close, since dropping a lens whose findings another role also reported is the cheapest way to remove it.

finding: The section's premise — "The prior-round carry re-presents a role's unresolved work in its next-round prompt. Deactivating that role would drop the work out of the loop" — is not what the code does. `loadReviewRoundState` collects rows from all recorded rounds into one `prevFindings` list; `runReview` turns it into a single `summary` (`buildFindingsSummary`) that `buildReviewPrompts` appends to *every* role prompt identically. The carry is one role-agnostic block, not a per-role re-presentation, which the section half-admits two sentences later ("the round-carry's dedup key ... carries no role at all"). Deactivating a role therefore does not drop its findings out of the next round's prompts at all — it drops the lens. A new exit-4 refusal is being justified by a mechanism tp does not have.
